claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, let me ask: **Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children do you have, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child. His name is Alex and he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to ask you some questions about your situation with Alex.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex.

**Do you live with Alex, or if you don't live with him, do you pay at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount (or more) towards his upkeep, such as for food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a few more questions to make sure I have all the information I need.

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any residential accommodation paid for by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he has been in local authority care for a couple of months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is an important detail as it affects Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me more specifically - has Alex been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks? And does he spend any regular time at home with you, such as 24 hours or more per week, or perhaps 2 nights in a row each week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's been in care for more than 8 weeks - it's been about 12 weeks now. But no, he doesn't come home regularly. He's there full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Under UK Child Benefit rules, when a child goes into local authority care for more than 8 weeks, you usually stop being entitled to Child Benefit. Since Alex has been in care for about 12 weeks now, you've exceeded this time limit.

There are some exceptions that could allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit - for example, if Alex was spending at least 24 hours per week at home with you, or spending 2 consecutive nights each week at home. However, since you've confirmed that Alex is in care full-time and doesn't come home regularly, these exceptions don't apply to your situation.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for instance, if he starts spending regular time at home - you should contact HMRC to discuss whether you might become eligible again.

However, the claimant has confirmed that Alex does not come home regularly and is in care full-time. Since Alex has been in care for more than 8 weeks and does not spend regular time at home (no 24 hours per week at home, and no 2 nights in a row each week or 7+ days in a row at home), the claimant does not qualify for an exception to the 8-week rule. Therefore, the claimant is INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.
